subject.title: [Bug]: Memory detection skips macOS (darwin) — os.freemem() / os.totalmem() never reported to agent on non-Linux platforms

question: Should macOS startup optimization hints target all Apple Silicon Macs like Linux ARM, or only low-memory darwin hosts?
rationale: The code change is small, but broad Apple Silicon targeting could show Pi/VM-style guidance on high-memory Macs unless maintainers choose a narrower macOS policy.

options.title: Low-memory darwin only
options.body: Add darwin support only for genuinely constrained Macs, keep Linux ARM behavior unchanged, update wording to be platform-neutral, and cover darwin low/high-memory tests.

options.title: Match Linux ARM behavior
options.body: Treat all darwin ARM hosts as startup-tuning targets and make that broader Apple Silicon policy explicit in copy and tests.

options.title: Keep Linux-only hints
options.body: Reject or defer macOS startup hints if this guidance should remain limited to Linux low-power hosts for now.

recommendation.title: Low-memory darwin only
recommendation.body: Add darwin support only for genuinely constrained Macs, keep Linux ARM behavior unchanged, update wording to be platform-neutral, and cover darwin low/high-memory tests.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc introduced the startup optimization helper and original Linux-only target policy.
